You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task note: task-05ea8da2

## Verified rule (solved 2026-10-21)

Input is partitioned into equal rectangular panels by full-width/full-height separator lines. A panel with a non-background pattern is the template: copy its contents into every panel, preserving the separators and the panel background. In the demonstrated task there were 2 rows × 2 columns of panels; the upper-left 5×6 region held a sparse pattern and the other three regions were background, so the output tiled the 5×6 template into all four regions. In the solved test there were 2 rows × 3 columns of 5×4 panels; the bottom-right panel contained a 5×4 pattern and all other panels were background. Correct output replicated that pattern into every panel.

How to apply on recurrence: identify full separator rows/columns (separator color differs from dominant field), split at separators, infer panel dimensions and locate the unique populated pattern panel; replicate it across all equal-sized panels, leaving separator lines as-is. Verify dimension compatibility and pattern alignment.

Evidence, demo 1 (11×13): separator row 5 and column 6, color 2. The 5×6 upper-left template was replicated into all four 5×6 regions; output retained row/column separators. Template rows:
`[[6,3,3,3,7,3],[3,7,6,3,3,6],[3,3,3,3,3,0],[3,3,3,7,3,3],[3,7,3,3,9,3]]`.

Solved test (11×14): separators row 5, color 3, and columns 4, 9, color 3. Six 5×4 panels, background 5. Bottom-right seed pattern:
`[[6,0,9,9],[6,1,5,5],[5,5,5,5],[5,1,0,9],[5,5,6,5]]`.
This was tiled over all six panels; resulting 11×14 submission was accepted correct (zero wrong attempts).
